matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the integer values of both sides, find the numeric difference, then search for a single‑stick move that changes the values by exactly that difference, ensuring the resulting symbols remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which stick to move; start by quantifying the imbalance.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without checking that the change matches the numeric difference, leading to a still‑incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, relocate one of V’s diagonal sticks to cross the other, turning V into X and increasing its value by 5 while keeping the source character valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between sides is 5 and a V is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of turning V into X when the equation is off by 5, and instead moving a stick elsewhere that does not fix the imbalance.

matchstick.title: Swap I and V in IV to make VI (adds 2)
matchstick.principle: When the imbalance is exactly 2 and the pattern IV appears, move the vertical stick of the I onto the V to form VI, increasing the value by 2 while preserving both numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference is 2 and the right‑hand side contains the numeral IV.
matchstick.example: Missing the chance to change IV to VI when the equation is off by 2, leaving the equation unsolved.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is present and the numeric imbalance can be corrected by decreasing the right‑hand side, turn '+' into '-' by removing its vertical stick and use that stick to create an extra I where it adds the needed value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains '+' and the required correction is a reduction of the right side by 1.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' without providing the missing vertical stick, resulting in an incomplete minus sign.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: When the equation is off by an even amount (or any integer) and there are numerals containing multiple I's, relocate a vertical stick from one of those I's to create a new I elsewhere, decreasing the source numeral by 1 and increasing the target numeral by 1; this changes the overall result by 2 (or the appropriate amount given the operators).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you have at least one numeral with extra I's and moving a single I can balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Taking the only vertical stick from an isolated I, which destroys that numeral, instead of moving a stick from a numeral that has spare I's.

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: If a minus sign appears and the numeric imbalance is large, move a horizontal stick from a numeral that can spare one (e.g., from an I or V) to the minus sign, turning it into an equals sign, while adjusting the source numeral accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains '-' and you need to increase the left side or decrease the right side by the value of a horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Trying to turn '-' into '=' by taking a stick from X, which would leave X invalid.

matchstick.title: Relocate minus sign to a different position
matchstick.principle: When a minus sign is present, consider moving its single horizontal stick to a new location, creating a minus sign elsewhere and possibly converting the original location into another operator, provided all resulting symbols stay valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When swapping the positions of '-' and another operator could resolve the imbalance.
matchstick.example: Moving the minus sign's stick to a spot that does not form a valid operator, leaving the equation with missing or malformed operators.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: If you need to change a minus sign into a plus sign, you must also relocate a vertical stick to the same location, because a plus sign requires both a horizontal and a vertical stick; otherwise the operator is incomplete.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the solution requires turning '-' into '+' to adjust the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Changing '-' to '+' by only adding a horizontal stick, leaving the plus sign missing its vertical component.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If the equation can be balanced by exchanging the positions of the minus and equality signs, move one horizontal stick from the existing '=' to the '-' location, turning the original '=' into '-' and the original '-' into '=', thereby preserving a valid equality sign while swapping the operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance suggests that swapping '-' and '=' would correct the equation, and both operators are present.
matchstick.example: Leaving the equality sign unchanged when swapping it with the minus sign would solve the puzzle, resulting in a still‑incorrect equation.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from the equality sign, simultaneously create a new equality sign elsewhere (e.g., by adding a stick to a minus sign) so that the equation still contains exactly one valid '=' operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a stick from '=', verify that the original location remains a valid operator (e.g., '-' or '+') and that another location gains a new '=', preserving exactly one equality sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=', turning it into '-', and not creating a new '=', leaving the equation without a proper equality operator.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, overlooking that some numerals need all their sticks to stay valid.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only remove sticks from numerals that have redundant sticks (e.g., I in a group of I's) or from numerals that can transform into another valid numeral after losing a stick.

matchstick.description: Providing an incomplete equation after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model truncates the output or forgets to include all parts of the original equation after transformation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always output the full equation, preserving the left‑hand side, operator, and right‑hand side, with only the intended characters altered.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick (resulting in an incomplete plus sign)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model adds a horizontal stick to turn '-' into '+', but forgets that '+' also needs a vertical stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting '-' to '+', also relocate a vertical stick to the same location to complete the plus sign.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa), creating an invalid numeral or operator
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats all sticks as interchangeable, ignoring the distinction between diagonal and vertical sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: only move vertical sticks to positions that require vertical orientation, and only move diagonal sticks to diagonal positions.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a horizontal stick from '=', turning it into '-', but does not create a new '=' elsewhere, breaking the equation's structure.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you move a stick from '=', ensure that the original location remains a valid operator (e.g., '-' or '+') and that another location gains a new '=', preserving exactly one equality sign.
